title: A Broke Blacksmith Just Got Drafted Into A Crafting Duel To Save A Stranger's Life . . . (Episode 3)
caption:
Overgeared episode 3 opens with Khan refusing to give Grid his ancestor's legendary armor. Then Grid is dragged into a crafting duel to free a stranger from a dungeon. Follow for episode 4!

#overgeared #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you enter the match to free Hu-Roy, or leave him to rot like Grid wanted? Why?

segments.say: Grid walks into an arena to save a stranger, and his opponent is a *liar* who already conned the Merrow Company.
To see how it got here, go back to the night Khan got patched *up*.
That night, Grid asks for the legendary armor as a reward, but Khan says no. It is a family *heirloom*, made by his own ancestor.
Only one man ever mastered it, a smith named *Pogma*.
But Khan says Pogma's chosen successor will one day walk through his door. Grid grins and says that is *him*. Modest as ever.
Then a legendary quest unlocks. Prove the legend, and the reward is the power to change the *world*.
So Grid yells that he will prove the legend, and demands Khan teach him *smithing*.
Khan agrees, but warns him the Merrow Company will *return*.
Meanwhile, the Merrow boss is losing patience, so Rabbit hires a smooth talker named *Hu-Roy*.
Hu-Roy strolls into the village and tells everyone to join Merrow, or sign the forge away. Win for *everybody*.
Grid watches him work. Something about him feels *off*.
But Khan fires back that the law is on his side. Locals get the news first, and Merrow hid it from *them*.
Hu-Roy swears he will tell the Earl about the cheating, and the villagers cheer him *on*.
Then Grid freezes. Hu-Roy is a *player*, steering the NPCs, and a new quest just opened for him.
Grid chases him down an alley and demands to know how he flipped the *quest*.
Hu-Roy shrugs. Help the villagers, and a hidden quest can trigger. Then he shares the quest with *Grid*.
Grid insists he is a hardcore veteran too, and they part with a few *insults*.
But Hu-Roy never meant to help Merrow. Guards stop him before he reaches the *Earl*.
Rabbit steps out and calls him a bad liar. The moment he betrayed Merrow, he gave up his *freedom*.
Rabbit never forgives a double cross.
The guards throw him in the dungeon, and the secret quest changes *again*.
It is brutal. He must stay logged in for fifty hours straight, or lose *everything*.
His record is twenty hours. If his brain waves spike, the game logs him out, and the quest is *over*.
The game asks if he wants to quit. His finger hovers, but he will not give *up*.

segments.text: I'll clear this quest no matter what.

segments.say: Meanwhile, at the game company, an emergency meeting begins. Quest B-408 is a hidden S-rank, and *nobody* expected it.
If Hu-Roy wins, he becomes the first player with two *jobs*. That would reshape the whole game.
The odds? About nine percent. His best login ever lasted just twenty *hours*. Damn, those odds are ugly.
Then comes the twist. Hu-Roy shared the quest with Grid, so the game treats Grid as his rescuer. And Grid has no *idea*.
Far from the dungeon, a girl with a rare class has a whole party begging her to join. She picks whoever kills the most *mobs*.
Then she copies a fighter's skill, and the system stores it. Another lovely day in an epic *class*.
She also holds an S-rank quest to take down a knight, and she finally thinks she can *clear* it.
Then Rabbit blocks her path and asks if the name Irina sounds *familiar*.
Irina is the name she used to fool the Merrow Company. She took the advance and vanished. Her real handle is Euphemina the *Duplicator*.
She says she is busy. He says she is not. That was no *request*.
Her new quest is a crafting match against a blacksmith. Win, and she earns fifteen hundred *gold*.
Back in the village, Grid hears Hu-Roy was arrested for treason against the *Earl*.
Then Rabbit knocks on Grid's door, polite as ever, and says the Merrow Company wants a *word*.
Grid says the damn fool can rot in there. But Khan reminds him Hu-Roy tried to protect the *village*.
So Rabbit offers a deal. A crafting match. If Grid wins, Merrow drops the forge and frees *Hu-Roy*.
Khan will not fight himself. He nominates Pogma's successor. Grid nearly *chokes*. Karma moves fast.
Grid snaps that nobody asked him. Then he sees the prize. Six hundred gold, about seventy-two thousand yen, *real* money.
Rabbit only smiles. He says Grid is no successor, and he plans to prove it in three *days*.
In the dungeon, Hu-Roy keeps counting down. Grid is his only way *out*.

segments.text: They can kiss my legendary class.

segments.say: Three days pass, and the whole town files into an arena for the *match*.
The host cheers it on, while the Merrow boss watches from the stands, sure he has already *won*.
Grid steps onto the sand. Khan and the villagers cheer him *on*.
Then his opponent waves to the crowd. It is Euphemina, the girl who conned Merrow, now fighting for them. Rabbit *owns* her.
At the game company, the staff are glued to the screens. The first second job rests on Grid's *shoulders*.
Euphemina walks up with a sweet hello, and Grid has one *question*.

segments.text: Gross, what are you, kid? Like twelve?

segments.say: She snaps that she is nineteen, and he says that is hard to *believe*.
They glare at each other until the host shouts, let the match *begin*.
The match begins, and Hu-Roy has less than eleven hours left. One wrong swing could cost him *everything*. Follow for episode 4!
